summary: CAST explicitly converts an expression to a named SQLite storage type.
documentation: CAST explicitly converts an expression to a named SQLite storage type. Converting integer text to INTEGER removes textual formatting such as leading zeroes. NULL remains NULL.
inputs: An expression and target type name.
caution: SQLite conversions are permissive: invalid or partly numeric text can yield a numeric result instead of an error. CAST is not input validation.
scenarios: Convert already validated integer text for a numeric report.
Normalize numeric export fields before comparing totals.
Make a conversion explicit instead of relying on column affinity.
title: Convert validated count text
problem: From imports(id INTEGER, count_text TEXT), return id and CAST(count_text AS INTEGER) as quantity, ordered by id. Non-NULL values are valid signed base-10 integer strings within the signed 32-bit range, possibly padded with spaces or zeroes. NULL remains NULL.
goal: Use CAST(... AS INTEGER) or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Convert only after the problem’s stated validation assumption.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT or WITH query against the supplied tables.
SELECT 1;
